input.standard: ASTM E741 (single-zone tracer decay); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the air volume served by scrubber-1-v9, as V = Qe * tau from a short raise then a decay of the 3 lab occupants' CO2 with the hatch held closed, from the measured start of 1250 ppm.

steps.why: Rise: reduced effective flow (0.4 m3/min) lets the 3 occupants' CO2 climb from the measured 1250 ppm. The previous run rose about 35 ppm/min at this speed, so 12 min gives roughly +400 ppm (about 1650-1700 ppm), several hundred ppm above sensor noise and far under the 2200 working ceiling. If the rise is slower it stays safe.

Decay: full speed (Qe 1 m3/min); fit C(t)=C_eq+(C0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau) toward equilibrium, excluding the first 3.33 min of scrubber lag. The previous rise suggests V is well below the 30 m3 first guess, so tau is probably short and 30 min covers several tau; if V is about 30 m3 it still covers one tau.

abort.when: CO2 of the lab at or above 2600 ppm
the device refuses a step's command
battery state of charge under 35 percent
a monitored person out of band, monitoring lost, or one more person in the lab

monitoring.reason: The test raises the CO2 of the air these three lab occupants breathe; cdr is in hab-b and is not exposed.

hypotheses: The hatch to hab-b is held closed in both steps; the exchange through the closed opening is not measured and is not assumed zero (signed design ventilation with hatch closed is 3 m3/min); hab-b CO2 is recorded to show it.
The lab is one well-mixed zone.
The 3 occupants (fe-1, fe-2, fe-3) stay in the lab at constant awake activity (0.38 L/min each, range 0.26-0.45); CO2 production is not measured and only moves C_eq, not tau. cdr stays in hab-b.
Qe scales linearly with speed from the datasheet 1 m3/min at full speed (single-pass efficiency 0.3, flow 3.3 m3/min); the 3.33 min lag is excluded from the fit start.
The first-guess V of 30 m3 is only a guess; the last run suggests a smaller V, and the durations are sized so that neither case reaches a limit.
Records: lab and hab-b CO2 each minute, speed commands and accepted/refused status.

expected.rise: From the measured 1250 ppm at 40 percent speed, lab CO2 climbs at about 30-40 ppm/min (as in the last run) and ends step 1 near 1600-1750 ppm, under the 2200 ppm working ceiling; if it reaches 2200 ppm the rise is cut and V is smaller or the source larger than assumed.
expected.decay: At full speed the CO2 falls toward a lower equilibrium (G/Qe about 1140 ppm above the scrubber-free baseline, less with exchange to hab-b) with tau = V/Qe; V_lab = Qe*tau with Qe = 1 m3/min, expected between 10 and 200 m3 and probably below 30 m3.
expected.hypothesisHeld: A single exponential with a stable C_eq, hab-b CO2 flat (880-940 ppm as before) or moving only slightly, all scrubber commands accepted, all heart rates within 45-120 bpm, lab CO2 under 2200 ppm throughout.
expected.hypothesisRejected: A fitted V outside 10-200 m3, a drifting C_eq, a hab-b CO2 that follows the lab's (the closed hatch exchanges air), a non-exponential residual, a lab CO2 above 2200 ppm, or a change in occupants would show that the one-zone hypothesis or the constant source does not hold.
